note: MicroModel chains of the Core Brain (guide 4.1; step P7). Read by nmbrain::chain::ChainBook and validated with named faults. Each chain is an ordered list of nodes; a node names its role (one of the four slots router, embedder, reranker, writer, or a decision, reasoning or verifier node), the fields of its controlled input (takes, in order) and the one field it emits. Seed fields every chain starts with: task (the task description) and parts (the parts handed up by G2). The chain's output field is the refined final output; every other field and every hop stays in the internal log. A reasoning node collaborates and never emits the output field. Version 2 (Stage 5 WP-C2, Luis's decision of 2026-11-22: keep the four chain names, re-express the hops in the Nano's own jobs, keep the earlier version in history): every node also names the Nano job it serves and the MicroModel that serves it (job and micromodel, read by the routing record and the interface; the roles, inputs and outputs are unchanged, so every chain check and node binding of version 1 still holds). Designs: Luis Jake Gabriel III, Gavriel Technologies.

router.what: the drones' read of the request and the pieces at the reader's first layers: kind, aspects, relations and the jobs to route

embedder.what: meaning recall and the embedder's meaning read of code against code close calls (routing record)

reranker.what: the judge's close calls and pair reads (prose duels, leader-only close call), calibrated by content-free reads

reasoning.what: the reader's joint read of related pieces (definition and use, ties), the label readout

writer.what: the writer's notes, summaries and outline (at idle) and its synthesis

verifier.what: sufficiency: does the set answer the request (one-word judgement)

decision.what: G2's gate and selection: settle, withhold, or order more reading

chains.description: find where a symbol, file, definition or module is located in the code base and which parts call or use it
explain how and why a piece of code works, what a component does and how its parts relate
propose a change, fix, addition or refactor to the code and state what it touches
check whether a claim, answer or result is supported by the code, its tests or its build output
